name: Leutasch
kurzbeschreibung: Vastly spread-out village community in the Gaistal valley, featuring over 400 km of hiking trails and the famous Leutascher Geisterklamm.
beschreibung:
Overview

Leutasch is an expansive high-valley alpine municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district and an exceptional natural centerpiece of the renowned Region Seefeld. Situated at an altitude of 1,136 metres along a sun-drenched 16-kilometre valley basin between the Wetterstein range to the north and the Mieming Chain to the south, the community comprises roughly 2,500 residents scattered across 24 scenic hamlets. Leutasch has preserved its authentic Tyrolean agricultural character and rural serenity. Celebrated across Europe as a premier nordic skiing haven, the valley is famed for the dramatic Leutasch Spirit Gorge (Geisterklamm), the alpine pasture paradise of the Gaistal, and its literary heritage linked to author Ludwig Ganghofer.

History

Systematic settlement of this heavily forested high valley commenced during the 12th century through land clearing directed by the Augustinian canons of Polling Abbey in Bavaria. The locality first appeared in written records in 1178 under the name Liutaische. For centuries, inhabitants sustained themselves through subsistence dairy farming, timber trade, and lime burning. The Gothic parish church of Saint Mary Magdalene in Oberleutasch and the church of Saint John the Baptist in Unterleutasch anchor the valley's sacred traditions. In the late 19th century, celebrated author Ludwig Ganghofer chose the secluded Gaistal valley as his writing retreat; at his Hubertus hunting lodge he penned classic novels including "Das Schweigen im Walde". In the modern era, reliable snowfall made Leutasch a premier hub for cross-country skiing.

Getting There

Leutasch enjoys straightforward, scenic travel accessibility. Motorists approaching from Germany travel toll-free via Garmisch-Partenkirchen and Mittenwald directly into Unterleutasch. From Innsbruck, drivers follow the A12 Inntal Autobahn to exit Zirl-Ost, ascending the Zirler Berg via the B177 highway to Seefeld, continuing along the scenic L14 regional road directly into Leutasch. Rail passengers arrive at international ICE stations in Seefeld in Tirol or Mittenwald, from where frequent public buses operated by the VVT network connect all 24 hamlets throughout the valley.

Tips

Walking through the Leutasch Spirit Gorge (Leutascher Geisterklamm) is an unforgettable adventure: an engineered 800-metre steel walkway hangs boldly above the roaring rapids of the Leutascher Ache deep inside the limestone canyon. In winter, the valley becomes a world-class nordic skiing paradise with direct access to the Region Seefeld's 245-kilometre groomed cross-country trail network. During summer, the Gaistal valley beckons cyclists and hikers to explore traditional alpine dairy huts like the Hämmermoosalm and Gaistalalm. Culture lovers should tour the Ganghofer Museum in Kirchplatzl, while the Alpenbad Leutasch leisure pool offers restorative wellness.
